_about: The meadow: its size and layout, the fog round it, what grows and how fast, the forest and its trees, and how much room the game keeps for things.

meadow._about: Where everything is, in metres; home is at 0, 0.

GRAVITY.about: how fast falling things speed up, m/s each second; raise it and jumps and throws come down sooner

WORLD_HALF.about: The meadow reaches this far from the centre, inside a fence. Prosio's home with its oven is in the middle; each kind of food grows in its own part of the meadow (see REGIONS), so he has to go out and fetch it.

HOME.about: where his home is, in metres: the middle of the meadow

POND.about: The pond: the only water to drink. It is round, and too deep to walk into.

POND_RADIUS.about: how far the pond reaches from its middle, in metres

PATH_ENDS.about: Paths from home out to each region, as straight segments; they wander a little when drawn.

MAP_CELL.about: What Prosio has seen of the meadow, for the map: it is in squares of MAP_CELL, and everything within SIGHT of him is uncovered as he goes.

SIGHT.about: further with plenty of vitamins, less without (see EAGLE_SIGHT and DIM_SIGHT in diet.json)

FOG_START.about: Beyond the edge of the meadow lies a thick dark fog: it starts FOG_START metres past the edge and is solid FOG_THICK metres further. Nobody walks into it, but an animal thrown far enough flies into it and is lost: it comes back later at home, like any other that is gone.

FOG_THICK.about: metres from where the fog starts to where it is solid

FOG_LOST.about: how far past the edge a flying animal is lost (or as soon as it comes down beyond it)

growing._about: What grows, how much of it there is, and how fast it comes back.

FOOD_BUDGET.about: Food is scarce. Of each kind there is never more in the whole meadow than FOOD_BUDGET calories' worth, counted at full size: so ten pumpkins, a dozen sheaves of wheat, forty-odd apples, eighty bunches of berries. That is a ceiling, not a promise. What is picked does not come straight back: after a wait a new one sprouts, small, and grows to its full size, which differs a little from one to the next. Picked early it is worth less.

MUSHROOM_BUDGET.about: mushrooms are so light there would be far too many

UNRIPE.about: the share of its calories a thing has when it has only just sprouted

SIZE_SPREAD.about: how much one thing's full size can differ from the usual, either way

BERRY_REGROW.about: seconds until a picked bush starts another bunch

MAX_APPLES.about: apples on one tree, with those lying under it

APPLE_REGROW.about: seconds between a tree's new apples

APPLE_GROW.about: seconds for apples to ripen on the tree

APPLE_LIFE.about: seconds a fallen apple lies there before it rots away

EGG_LIFE.about: seconds a laid egg lies there before it is gone

MAX_EGGS.about: eggs lying about at once, all over the meadow: well under the budget

FOOD_REGROW.about: Seconds until a new one sprouts where one was picked (somewhere in this range), and then to grow to full size. apples are not replanted: new ones grow on the trees the turkeys lay new ones only he puts spears there

FOOD_SIZE.about: How big each is on the ground. Only a pumpkin is big enough to bump into.

SALT_ROCKS.about: big rocks in the goat hills with rock salt growing on them (salt is no energy, so it has no budget)

SALT_REGROW.about: seconds until another lump has grown

SALT_ROCK_RADIUS.about: how big a salt rock is on the ground, in metres

PEBBLE_PATCHES.about: Patches of pebbles for throwing: some in the goat hills, by the pond, and one each near home, the turkeys and the fields.

PEBBLE_REGROW.about: seconds until another has worked its way up

PEBBLE_PATCH_RADIUS.about: how big a patch of pebbles is, in metres

forest._about: Shaking a tree: standing right at it (no further than TREE_SHAKE_REACH from its trunk) and facing it (within TREE_SHAKE_ANGLE either side) he takes hold of it with both hooves and shakes it, as hard as his arms are strong (STRONG and NOODLE_ARMS in prosio.json, skills). The crown shakes that much, and that many apples come down.

VIEW_SLOPE.about: Where trees may stand. The camera always looks from the south, and from above (rising VIEW_SLOPE metres back for every metre up): so a tree's leaves hide a strip of ground to the north of its trunk, from under their lowest to beyond their highest, as wide as its crown (see tree_cover). A tall tree hides ground ten metres behind it. Two rules come of that: nothing is planted where it would stand in front of something that has to stay in view: a path, a field, a building, a hive, a salt rock, a berry bush, food on the ground (see hides_something); and what is put down after the trees (bushes, mushrooms, nuts, salt) goes only where no tree stands in front of it (see hidden_by_tree).

FOREST_TREES.about: trees in the forest (besides the apple trees),

FOREST_SPACING.about: each at least this far from the next,

FOREST_EDGE.about: thinning to this share of the trees at its edge

FOREST_STUMPS.about: mossy stumps and fallen logs in the forest

STUMP_RADIUS.about: how big a stump or a fallen log is on the ground, in metres

CLEARINGS.about: The forest's clearings, and the trail that joins them to the path from home (PATH_ENDS[.Forest]).

CLEARING_RADIUS.about: how far each clearing reaches from its middle, in metres

TRAILS.about: the forest's trails, each a straight run from one point to another, in metres

TREE_SHAKE_REACH.about: metres between him and the trunk

TREE_SHAKE_ANGLE.about: 30 degrees either side of where he faces

TREE_SHAKE_APPLES.about: apples that come down for arms of ordinary strength

trees._about: Trees drawn from models: each kind's height and crown width (metres, before a tree's own size), which models it takes, how much one tree differs from the next, and its leaves.

TREE_HEIGHT.about: Each kind's height (metres, before a tree's own size), how wide its crown is (its radius), and its two models.

TREE_CROWN.about: how wide each kind's crown is: its radius, in metres

TREE_PICK.about: the models each kind is drawn from; a tree takes one of them by its number

TREE_WIDTH.about: how much wider or narrower a tree may be than its kind,

TREE_SHADE.about: and how much lighter or darker its leaves may be

TREE_LEAVES.about: Leaves for each kind (a tree's own shade is laid over them).

limits._about: How many of each thing the game keeps room for (it allocates nothing while playing). Raise one only if the meadow needs more.

MAX_ROUNDS.about: round things standing in the world at once, a count: trees, rocks, bushes, hives, stations and what he builds

MAX_FOODS.about: food growing or lying about at once

MAX_PARTICLES.about: bits of dust, sparks and splashes in the air at once; when it is full the oldest goes

MAX_DECOR.about: grass tufts, flowers and ferns, there only to look at

plants._about: How big the grass clumps, ferns, low bushes and fallen logs are drawn.

GRASS_SIZE.about: how big a clump of grass is drawn, against its model (0.4 m tall)

SHRUB_SIZE.about: a low bush under the forest trees (1.2 m tall as modelled)

LOG_LENGTH.about: a fallen log, from end to end
